title: world-heavyweight-acwa-atlantic-1999
label: "Showstoppa" Steve Starr

won.source: The champion's own billing on the promotion's own 22 December 1999 broadcast, recapping that he inserted himself into a three-way dance for the title against the defending champion, The Rose, at an outside interfederation pay-per-view, and won it there. The pay-per-view broadcast itself is not part of this record.

note: Still billed champion as of the promotion's own last document held in this record, 22 December 1999.

title: world-heavyweight-acwa-atlantic-1999
label: Chad Shakespeare

won.source: Won the World Heavyweight Championship in a four-man Four Corners match at "Take No Prisoners," pinning Steve Starr after a diving headbutt.

note: Made one successful title defense before the promotion's own president announced he was vacating the championship after an injury sustained in an unsanctioned attack.

title: world-heavyweight-acwa-atlantic-1999
label: William Craven

won.source: Won a ten-man, double-ring cage match by retrieving the vacant championship belt at "Ground Zero."

note: Lost the title to The Rose by submission at "Painful Declaration."

title: world-heavyweight-acwa-atlantic-1999
label: The Rose

won.source: Won the World Heavyweight Championship from William Craven by submission at "Painful Declaration."

note: Retained the championship in a Triple Threat main event against William Craven and Steve Starr at the promotion's own first pay-per-view. A later broadcast recaps this reign ending in an outside interfederation pay-per-view three-way dance, where Steve Starr inserted himself and won the title.

end.source: Recorded from a later broadcast's own recap of the loss, since the pay-per-view broadcast itself is not part of this record.

title: world-tag-team-acwa-atlantic-1999
label: Love Muscle

won.source: Won the World Tag Team Championship from the Alliance of Violence by submission at "Take No Prisoners."

note: No further title change survives in the documents read for this record; a December 1999 broadcast announces a tournament to fill the championship, suggesting the team's own mid-year breakup left it inactive, but no formal vacation notice was found.

title: world-tag-team-acwa-atlantic-1999
label: Alliance of Violence

won.source: Recorded from the promotion's own billing entering "Take No Prisoners," which frames the Alliance of Violence as the promotion's own only World Tag Team Champions, of four months' standing.

note: Lost the title to Love Muscle by submission at "Take No Prisoners."

title: television-acwa-atlantic-1999
label: Joe Gonzo

won.source: Won an eight-man tournament final against Sabbath by submission at the promotion's own first pay-per-view.

note: The promotion's own earlier 1999 Television Championship history (at least one prior tournament and vacancy) is attested in documents not structured for this record.

title: television-acwa-atlantic-1999
label: Maxx Madhouse

won.source: No document read for this record states when Maxx Madhouse first won the championship; he is attested only as its defending champion, billed as the greatest Television Champion in the promotion's own history.

note: Lost the belt to Joe Gonzo in the ring, but the promotion's own owner vacated the championship immediately afterward, ruling the finish tainted by interference and excessive violence.

title: world-heavyweight-acwa-atlantic-1999
label: "Showstoppa" Steve Starr

won.source: Recorded from the promotion's own billing, which frames Starr as the reigning World Heavyweight Champion entering the season-opening card, having regained the title from Wild Fire in a cage match before the record read for this wing begins.

note: Lost the title to Chad Shakespeare in a four-man Four Corners match at "Take No Prisoners."
